additional_info.subject: ID0439318-DC/Si-D/CZ-[ MP / R7 170002211] Circuit breaker Issue CRM:02888000161
additional_info.body:
Hi Milan,
To troubleshoot the QA1 we have to check these steps:
My first as always is to check if the XD9.1 is inserted tightly. These are those loose connectors.
Second is by applying (or checking) 24V on the QA29, we should be able to get 230V until the input of both L+ and ON in the MA1.
If we apply 24V on the A1-A2 and the contact 11-14 doesn't close then we need to replace QA29, same process with QA28
Next thing is to check 24V on the Under voltage relay and if the QA1 feedback contact is closing.
The 24V to the UVR are supplied by QA26:
Next question, when you reach the site, what is the LED color of the ACT and TRIP in the QA1? (seen from the front)
If both LEDs are on then that means MA1 is faulty and needs replacement.
If everything above checks out properly and it still doesn't work (230V in MA1, QA26 sending 24V, 24V in KF5 - first photo and KF2, for QA29 and QA28 - second photo). Please measure on the output of the QA1 if any phase is not having the 230/380V:
If we don't have a phase or multiple phases then we need to replace the QA1 but MA1 should not be necessary or the UVR.
If QA26 is not sending the 24V for the UVR, then we need to check which of these lines is not getting 24V:
If all of them checks out fine and we still don't have 24V in the output (24) then we need to replace the QA26.
I don't think it's the feedback of the QA1 since we don't have the error called "Failure in Feedback line".
Usually when we have these kind of problems it's the MA1 but let's prove it.
My recommendation is to take a spare MA1, QA26, QA28/29 (they are the same) and UVR. Let me know if you think you should take a QA1, I can recommend it too.
Let me know your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0439318-DC/Si-D/CZ-[ MP / R7 170002211] Circuit breaker Issue CRM:02888000161
additional_info.body:
Hello Francisco,
Thank you very much for the quite comprehensive troubleshooting manual. Let´s go through it!
XD9.1 checked. Everything seems correctly connected and pushed inside the connector proreply.
On A1 of QA28 I measure around 7,34 volts same goes for QA29. When I bring voltage (24Volts) to A1 QA28 and QA29 lights up. When QA29 lights up MA1 motor engages for the first time and shortly after for the second time. We can see this behaviour when the doors are closed as well. Therefore I think QA28 and QA29 are ok.
Next thing is to check 24V on the under-voltage relay and if the QA1 feedback contact is closing.
We have 24 Volts here
XD34 6C and 6D –>24Volts
We have 0Volts here in both cases doors closed and open
XD34 7A and 7B
The 24V to the UVR are supplied by QA26:
Sirius seems ok.
Next question, when you reach the site, what is the LED color of the ACT and TRIP in the QA1? (seen from the front)
ACT is flashing green it only stay green when motor is engaged. TRIP has no light
There is no voltage behind QA1.
Just to make sure, does it mean we need to replace QA1 only? Can you please send me MLFB so we can order it?
I will atach photos under ticket documents.
Thank you again for your support here!
Best,
Milan

additional_info.subject: ID0439318-DC/Si-D/CZ-[ MP / R7 170002211] Circuit breaker Issue CRM:02888000161
additional_info.body:
Hi Milan,
Thank you for the reply.
If we had a problem in the feedback line, we would see a specific error Failure in Feedback line, which is when we have the circuit breaker closed and have output voltage but feedback is open.
I recommend you to take spare QA1 and MA1. Everything points to the fact that the circuit breaker is not closing but that is also possible if MA1 is not working properly.
I can only make a suggestion here in order to avoid losing as much time as possible but feel free to do as you wish. Replacing the MA1 is always faster and easier, but then if it's the main breaker that is really not closing then we would still need to prove that MA1 is also faulty by putting the old back.
Let me know if you need any support and schedule with 1 day in advance please.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
